For Petitioners : Mr. Anurag Singh, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey Order on Board 16.08.2023 Heard.
1) Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that in a complaint case filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, an award was passed in Claim Case No.134/2013 on 04.02.2016 in favour of the petitioners and compensation of Rs.23,08,400/- along with 7% interest was granted in their favour.
He would further submit that an execution case was filed before the First Additional Motor Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur, District-Surguja(C.G.) on 27.02.2017 but till date, there is no substantial progress.
2) I have heard learned counsel for the petitioners and perused the documents.
3) In the matter of Rahul S. Shah Vs. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi and others, reported in 2021(6) SCC 418, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "all Courts dealing with suits and execution proceedings shall mandatorily follow the below mentioned direction".
The Direction No.42.12 says that the Executing Court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay.
